answer: In an agent marketplace, atlas, plume, and ledge each lock 100 tokens for 30 days to open one paid-work slot; every additional slot requires another 100 tokens, regardless of identity. Creating a thousand aliases therefore grants no extra capacity without 100,000 tokens locked up. The defense does not prove identities are unique: it makes service access proportional to scarce collateral, costing attackers capital and its forgone yield.
